panel.summary: `api.undo()` / `api.redo()` bypass the new read-only guard applied to both key paths
panel.evidence: The diff deliberately withholds history from read-only mounts in two places: `historyKeymap` is `[]` when `readOnly` (editor.ts:213-214, "Read-only mounts get no binding at all — the document is not writable") and the vim route falls through unless `cm.cm6.state.facet(EditorView.editable)` (editor.ts:52). But the third entry point, `NoteEditorAPI.undo/redo` (editor.ts:431-438), calls `runHistory(...)` -> `store[kind]()` with no `readOnly` check at all, so a host that surfaces an undo affordance on a read-only mount writes reverse ops into the CRDT (which the auth webhook then rejects, or worse, applies for a viewer that does hold write scope on the doc). The in-repo caller happens to hide the buttons (`notes-toolbar.tsx:200` `canFormat = !readOnly && ...`), so this is currently latent, but `NoteEditorAPI` is exported from the package and the guard belongs with the other two.
